t: The Neo-Sumerian Empire, or Third Dynasty of Ur, revived Sumerian rule in southern Mesopotamia after the Akkadian collapse.
Its bureaucracy recorded the economy on tens of thousands of tablets, and its law code is the oldest that survives.
Amorite incursions, grain shortages and breakaway governors weakened it until Elam sacked Ur c. 2004 BCE.
dyk: The Code of Ur-Nammu, some three centuries older than Hammurabi's, punished many offences with monetary fines rather than physical penalties.
ev: Ur-Nammu founds the Third Dynasty of Ur after Utu-hegal expels the Gutians
Shulgi becomes king and expands and centralises the state
Shulgi's long reign ends; under his successors the empire begins to decline
Elamite forces sack Ur and carry the last king, Ibbi-Sin, into captivity
